action: No action needed; for awareness. NebuSec says all the exploits it describes were patched by the time of publication.
date_note: NebuSec's write-up is dated 20 November 2026; The Hacker News reported it on 21 November.
exec: Security researchers say a chain of flaws in Meta's Muse AI agent exposed users' private chats and stored memories; NebuSec says all were patched before publication.
plain: Researchers at NebuSec showed that a booby-trapped web page opened by Meta's Muse assistant could be used to take a user's chat history and memories. NebuSec says the flaws were fixed before it published.

sources.name: NebuSec: Hacking Muse: Stealing Private Chats Through Browser Use

summary: NebuSec says it chained weaknesses in Meta's Muse agent: a Chromium browser flaw gave code execution in the agent's container, weaknesses in the Sentinel outbound-request check let chat history and memories leave without an approval prompt, and a Linux kernel exploit gave root in the user's VM, exposing credential storage. NebuSec says all exploits were patched by publication; The Hacker News says Meta has not publicly confirmed.
title: NebuSec: malicious web page chain let researchers take Meta Muse users' private chats; says all fixed

validation.note: NebuSec (the researchers) is the only origin of the findings and the patch claim; The Hacker News relays it and says Meta has not publicly confirmed the fixes or commented. Both pages read; Meta statement not found.

review.note: Read NebuSec and The Hacker News: title, date 20 Nov, chain and patch claim match. Status official/severity 2/corroborated overstated a researcher-only claim Meta has not confirmed; now claimed, severity 1, unconfirmed_claim.
